title: How to REALLY get a 6 pack (Top Abs Exercises for Bodybuilding)
summary: NH demonstrates his ab isolation exercises: an anchored crunch emphasizing the bottom stretch, a rotating oblique variant, decline crunches and bench leg raises. He argues abs must be trained directly and progressively overloaded rather than revealed by dieting. He keeps a year-round six-pack at 16-17% body fat.
claims: Compound lifts and bracing are not enough for abs; without direct isolation you get a weak pack that takes months of cutting to reveal
NH keeps a fully visible six-pack year-round at 16-17% body fat because he trains abs directly
The stretch is the most important factor for ab hypertrophy, and standard floor crunches with knees up miss it
Anchor your feet under a squat rack or heavy object and crunch, lowering under control past parallel without touching the floor to stretch the abs
As a teenager he did thousands of anchored crunches every day, which built his abs
Load crunches with a weight on the chest, or behind the head for a longer moment arm and more difficulty
Common crunch mistake: staying slouched forward; keep a straight spine and open the chest to stretch fully on the way down
Holding a raised crunch and rotating the trunk (optionally with a weight) hammers the obliques and lower abs
Decline bench crunches are probably the best ab exercise: the angle maximally stretches the abs, especially the lower abs, and they are easy to load or drop-set
Missing lower abs can be extra fat, but often they simply are not trained enough
Leg raises have a bad reputation on YouTube for supposedly not training the abs biomechanically, but anyone who has done them feels the abs work hard
Do leg raises with only the hips on the bench and the legs floating; supporting half the legs on the bench is cheating
Beginners start with knee raises, then straight-leg raises, then overload with ankle weights or a dumbbell between the feet
In leg raises the bottom stretch, catching the legs below the body, is the key zone; reaching vertical at the top matters little
No lower-ab growth may mean the volume is too low or the load too light
Do a set of leg raises or crunches after each bench press set; it saves time and does not hurt bench performance
Prefer six-pack 'long cuts' over dieting shortcuts; naturally built ab muscle is kept for good
Start ab isolation with 2-3 sets a week and build up, to avoid shocking the muscle
Progression example: bodyweight crunches once a week and knee raises another day, both supersetted
The number one way to grow a muscle is to target it in priority with isolation and progressively overload
The belief that only low body fat produces abs is false and leaves you with a pack you must flex to see
At 210 lb and 6 ft he has a year-round six-pack, which he credits to hard work, not genetics
Abs recover quickly and can be trained daily, but do not exhaust them the day before heavy deadlifts or squats or you risk your lumbar spine
Train abs every day or three times a week, every time you train
